descriptionChirho: Spatial and relational preposition/adverb indicating position or direction in front of someone or something, used both as a preposition with genitive ('before God,' 'before men') and as an adverb ('ahead,' 'in front'). Multilingual translations uniformly confirm a single core spatial-relational meaning: eng 'before/in front/ahead', spa 'delante de/delante/adelante', hin 'saamne/aage' (in front/ahead), arb 'amaam' (in front of), kor 'ap-eseo/apseo' (at the front/ahead), swa 'mbele ya/mbele' (in front of/ahead). Used for spatial position (Matt 5:24, before the altar), metaphorical presence (Matt 10:32-33, before my Father), and temporal priority (John 1:15, he was before me).
